t: You're at the Henry VII Chapel, the large Lady chapel at the far eastern end of Westminster Abbey. It is separated from the rest of the abbey by brass gates and a flight of stairs. Henry VII, the first Tudor monarch, paid for it through his will, and it carries his name. Among those buried here is Elizabeth Stuart, known as the Winter Queen, because her husband's reign as King of Bohemia lasted only one winter. Their selection helped set off the turmoil of the Thirty Years' War. Also buried here is James Scott, Earl of Dalkeith, a grandson of Charles II.
